subject: physics_2
question_text: Explain the formation of stationary waves in an air column enclosed in open pipe. Derive the equations for the frequencies of the harmonics produced.

verification.note: The 1+2+2+2+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it — the figure carries 0 marks because the question does not ask for a diagram. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. Physics hand-checked: an open pipe has a displacement antinode at each open end, so l = λ₁/2 gives n₁ = v/2l; the next modes give λ₂ = l (n₂ = 2n₁) and λ₃ = 2l/3 (n₃ = 3n₁); the ratio is 1 : 2 : 3 with ALL harmonics present. The book's spellings 'Harmonies' and 'Foundamental' are corrected.

recall_prompt: Say the derivation in order — the open-pipe boundary condition, then the fundamental, second and third harmonics, and the ratio.

steps.label: Open pipe, harmonics and overtones
lines: An organ pipe is a cylindrical tube
holding an air column. If both ends are
open, it is an open organ pipe.
Sound waves reflect at the ends of the
waves with an antinode at each open end
and at least one node between them.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The boundary condition — an antinode at each OPEN end — drives every mode that follows.
steps.why: At an open end the air is free to move, so the displacement there is maximum — an antinode. Every allowed mode of the pipe is just a wave pattern that puts an antinode at both ends.
common_mistakes: Placing a node at an open end — free air moves; open ends take antinodes.
Treating harmonic and overtone as the same word — the second harmonic is the FIRST overtone.

recall.must_convey: That an open pipe forms stationary waves with a displacement antinode at each open end.
accept: overtones are the frequencies above the fundamental

steps.memory_tip: Open end = air free to move = antinode. Both ends open, so both ends antinodes.

steps.label: The fundamental mode
steps.margin_note: The fundamental: an antinode at each open end, one node in the middle — half a wavelength in the pipe.
steps.why: The sketch shows the simplest pattern that satisfies the open-pipe boundary condition; the higher harmonics only add more node–antinode pairs to this picture.
common_mistakes: Closing one end of the pipe in the sketch — an open pipe has no end wall on either side.

recall.must_convey: That the fundamental mode has an antinode at each end and a node in the middle, with l = λ₁/2.
accept: draw the pipe with antinodes at both ends
half a wavelength fits the pipe
reject: n two equals two n one

steps.memory_tip: Antinode–node–antinode is half a wave — that is the whole fundamental picture.

steps.label: Fundamental frequency
lines: antinode at each end and one node
between them, so half a wavelength fits
With v the speed of sound in air:
steps.margin_note: Two marks: the fit l = λ₁/2, then n₁ = v/2l.
steps.why: The mode with the fewest nodes has the longest wavelength and so the lowest frequency — that is what makes it the fundamental. Every other mode is counted from this one.
common_mistakes: Writing l = λ₁/4 — the quarter-wave fit belongs to the CLOSED pipe; an open pipe fits half a wave.
Using the string speed √(T/μ) — the wave here is sound in air, speed v.

recall.must_convey: That half a wavelength fits the open pipe, so λ₁ = 2l and n₁ = v/2l.

steps.memory_tip: Open pipe fundamental: half a wave in the pipe, so 2l under the v.

steps.label: Second harmonic
lines: two nodes and three antinodes. One full
steps.margin_note: Two marks: λ₂ = l from the node count, then n₂ = 2n₁.
steps.why: Adding one node squeezes one more half-wavelength into the same length, so the wavelength drops and the frequency rises to exactly twice the fundamental — the counting is the derivation.
common_mistakes: Calling this the second overtone — it is the second HARMONIC but the FIRST overtone.
Writing λ₂ = 2l/3 — that is the third harmonic; the second fits exactly one wavelength.

recall.must_convey: That the second harmonic fits one full wavelength, λ₂ = l, giving n₂ = 2n₁.
accept: n two is twice n one

steps.memory_tip: One more node, one more half-wave: the pipe now holds a full wavelength.

steps.label: Third harmonic
lines: three nodes and four antinodes. Three
steps.margin_note: Two marks: λ₃ = 2l/3 from the fit, then n₃ = 3n₁.
steps.why: Each new mode adds one half-wavelength to the fit, so the frequencies climb in equal steps — this third step is what reveals the whole-number pattern the ratio states next.
common_mistakes: Writing l = 3λ₃/4 — the three-quarter fit belongs to the closed pipe; here three HALVES fit.
Slipping on the algebra: v ÷ (2l/3) is 3v/2l, not 2v/3l.

recall.must_convey: That three half-wavelengths fit, λ₃ = 2l/3, giving n₃ = 3n₁.
accept: n three is three times n one

steps.memory_tip: Count the halves: 1, 2, 3 half-waves — the frequencies follow the same count.

steps.label: The ratio
lines: fundamental and the next harmonics are
An open pipe produces all the harmonics
steps.margin_note: Final mark. The ratio AND the sentence — all harmonics are present.
steps.why: The unbroken whole-number ratio is the open pipe's signature; the closed pipe's ratio 1 : 3 : 5 skips the even numbers, and examiners set the two pipes against each other on exactly this line.
common_mistakes: Writing 1 : 3 : 5 — that is the CLOSED pipe. The open pipe gives every whole number.
Stopping at the ratio without saying all harmonics are present — that sentence is the physical conclusion.

recall.must_convey: That the harmonic frequencies are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 and all harmonics are present.
accept: one is to two is to three
even and odd harmonics both occur
reject: one is to three is to five

steps.memory_tip: Open pipe, open list: 1, 2, 3, … with nothing skipped.

insider_note: The pattern is one antinode-to-antinode fit per mode: 1, 2, 3 half-wavelengths. Keep the closed pipe's quarter-wave fits out of this answer — mixing the two costs the middle marks.
